question: The Scrum Master is a leader and servant in service to which of the following?
explanation: The Scrum Master serves the whole Scrum ecosystem: they help the Scrum Team become more effective and support the organization in adopting Scrum. They do not serve only the Developers or only the Product Owner.

question: The Product Owner is primarily responsible for defining the "What" of the product. Who is primarily responsible for determining the "How" of implementing the features of the product?
explanation: Developers are self-managing: they decide how to turn the selected work into a usable Increment. The Product Owner is accountable for value and Product Backlog ordering, not for prescribing the technical solution.

question: Who may be best positioned to decide who will be the Scrum Master for a new Scrum Team?

answers.text: The Developers and the Product Owner

explanation: Scrum does not prescribe a mandatory process for appointing a Scrum Master. The Developers and Product Owner, who will form the Scrum Team, are well positioned to assess whether the person can serve the team and enable Scrum.

question: When should Product Backlog refinement occur?

answers.text: At the start of each Sprint

explanation: The correct answer is « Continuously throughout the Sprint ». Refinement is an ongoing activity: Product Backlog items are broken down and clarified until they are transparent and small enough to be selected in Sprint Planning. It is neither a separate Scrum event nor a phase reserved for the Product Owner.

question: All Scrum Teams will have a Scrum Master and Product Owner.

answers.text: False. A Business Analyst can take on the same responsibilities of a Product Owner.
True. The Product Owner and Scrum Master must be a full time member to the Scrum Team.
True. Outcomes are affected by their level of participation and availability.
False. A Scrum Master is only needed if or when requested by the Developers.

explanation: The correct answer is « True. Outcomes are affected by their level of participation and availability. ». Value should be examined against the outcome sought for users, the organization, and the product, not merely the volume of features delivered. Product choices compare benefits, costs, risks, and available learning.

question: The Product Owner must invite stakeholders to the Sprint Retrospective.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Sprint Retrospective lets the Scrum Team inspect how it works — interactions, processes, tools, and its Definition of Done — and then plan the changes most useful to quality and effectiveness.

question: Which of the following best describes the topics discussed at Sprint Planning?

answers.text: How conditions have changed and how the Product Backlog should evolve.
Who is on the team and what team member roles will be.
What went wrong in the last Sprint and what to do differently this Sprint.
Why the work is valuable, what can be done, and how to do it.
What to do and who will do it.

explanation: The correct answer is « Why the work is valuable, what can be done, and how to do it. ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: The Definition of Ready is part of Scrum
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Definition of Ready is not an element prescribed by Scrum. A team may use a context-appropriate readiness criterion, but Scrum only requires items to be transparent enough for Developers to select and complete them in a Sprint.

question: During Sprint Planning, all Product Backlog Items must be decomposed to a definitive set of tasks for the Developers to complete
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: Select the correct timebox for each Scrum event

answers.text: Sprint Planning - 8 hours, Daily Scrum - 15 minutes, Sprint Review - 4 hours, Sprint Retrospective - 3 hours.
Sprint Planning-4 hours, Daily Scrum - 15 minutes, Sprint Review-4 hours, Sprint Retrospective-4 hours.
Sprint Planning - 4 hours, Daily Scrum - 15 minutes, Sprint Review - 8 hours, Sprint Retrospective - 4 hours.
Sprint Planning - 8 hours, Daily Scrum - 30 minutes, Sprint Review - 4 hours, Sprint Retrospective - 3 hours.

explanation: The correct answer is « Sprint Planning - 8 hours, Daily Scrum - 15 minutes, Sprint Review - 4 hours, Sprint Retrospective - 3 hours. ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: Who is responsible for monitoring the progress of work during a Sprint?
explanation: The correct answer is « Developers ». Developers monitor progress during the Sprint and adapt their plan toward the Sprint Goal. The Sprint Backlog is their living plan, and the Daily Scrum is specifically used to adjust it.

question: An Increment is...

answers.text: All work completed up to now, where there are no bugs present
All work that was carried out in the Sprint
All work that has happened up to the current point in time
The sum of the Done work during a Sprint, plus the work Done in earlier Sprints

explanation: The correct answer is « The sum of the Done work during a Sprint, plus the work Done in earlier Sprints ». An Increment adds to all previous Increments and must work with them. It is therefore not just the Sprint’s work: it is the integrated, completed version of the product at that point.

question: Before the first Sprint, the Product Backlog must contain everything we will develop for the product
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Product Backlog is emergent and evolves for as long as the product exists. It does not need to contain all work before the first Sprint: feedback, risk, and opportunities change both its content and level of detail.

question: Who can do the work to ensure the Product Backlog is refined to a state that it is useful? Select 2 answers.

answers.text: The Developers, with support from the Product Owner who is still accountable for it

explanation: The correct answers are « The Developers, with support from the Product Owner who is still accountable for it » and « The Product Owner ». The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the Scrum Team’s work. They do not direct Developers: they provide product direction and make value choices and Product Backlog ordering clear.

question: A Product Backlog is never complete

answers.text: False - A complete Product Backlog should be created before starting the first Sprint
True - As long as a product exists, its Product Backlog also exists

explanation: The correct answer is « True - As long as a product exists, its Product Backlog also exists ». The Product Backlog is emergent and evolves for as long as the product exists. It does not need to contain all work before the first Sprint: feedback, risk, and opportunities change both its content and level of detail.

question: The Scrum Master is accountable for the Product Backlog
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Scrum Master is accountable for Scrum Team effectiveness and establishing Scrum, but not for Product Backlog management or for doing the team’s work. Those accountabilities belong to the Product Owner and Developers respectively.

question: The Scrum Master and Product Owner accountabilities can both be held by 1 person
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Scrum Master and Product Owner accountabilities are distinct. Assigning both to one person risks creating a conflict between neutral enablement of Scrum and product value and prioritization decisions.

question: The Product Owner must attend the Sprint Retrospective
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Sprint Retrospective lets the Scrum Team inspect how it works — interactions, processes, tools, and its Definition of Done — and then plan the changes most useful to quality and effectiveness.

question: Which statement best describes a cross-functional team?

answers.text: The team has all competencies needed to accomplish the work
All members of the team have all the skills required to create the Product
The team has a good mix of skills

explanation: The correct answer is « The team has all competencies needed to accomplish the work ». A Scrum Team is cross-functional: it has or acquires the skills needed to create value in the Sprint. This capability reduces handoffs, waiting, and external dependencies.

question: Developers include which role(s)? Select all that apply.

answers.text: No other roles. Developer is one of the 3 accountabilities in Scrum

explanation: The correct answers are « Testers », « Software Architects » and « Business Analysts ». In Scrum, “Developers” means the people in the Scrum Team committed to creating any aspect of a usable Increment. It is not a specialty name: testers, architects, analysts, and other experts can therefore be Developers.

question: Which of the following best describes the Scrum Team?

answers.text: Composed of Developers, Product Owner, and Scrum Master.

explanation: The correct answers are « Self-organizing and cross-functional. » and « Composed of Developers, Product Owner, and Scrum Master. ». Developers are self-managing: they internally decide who does what, when, and how to turn selected work into a usable Increment. The Product Owner defines the need and value, but does not prescribe the technical solution.

question: What does it mean when the Developers are 'self-organizing'?

answers.text: They manage their own work towards the Sprint Goal.

explanation: The correct answer is « They manage their own work towards the Sprint Goal. ». Developers are self-managing: they internally decide who does what, when, and how to turn selected work into a usable Increment. The Product Owner defines the need and value, but does not prescribe the technical solution.

question: The entire Scrum Team is accountable for meeting the Sprint Goal.
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». The Sprint Goal is the Sprint’s single objective. It creates coherence and focus while leaving Developers flexibility about the precise work needed to achieve it; it does not guarantee that every initially selected item will be completed.

question: The Scrum Master is accountable for the Scrum Team.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Scrum Master is accountable for Scrum Team effectiveness and establishing Scrum, but not for Product Backlog management or for doing the team’s work. Those accountabilities belong to the Product Owner and Developers respectively.

question: The Definition of Done is a measure of the work in Scrum.
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». The Definition of Done formally describes the quality state an Increment must meet. It creates a shared understanding of what is truly complete: an item that does not meet it is neither an Increment nor releasable work.

question: During the Daily Scrum, if the Developers realize they may not meet the Sprint Goal, what should they do?

answers.text: Inform the Product Owner that the Sprint Goal cannot be met.
Adjust the Sprint Backlog to reflect new understanding.
Collaborate with the Product Owner to re-negotiate the scope of the Sprint Backlog.
Extend the Sprint to complete the remaining work.

explanation: The correct answer is « Collaborate with the Product Owner to re-negotiate the scope of the Sprint Backlog. ». The Daily Scrum is a fifteen-minute event for Developers. Its purpose is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the work plan; it is neither a status report to management nor a mandatory meeting for external parties.

question: At the end of the Sprint Retrospective, the Scrum Team identified some improvements that can be done. What should the Scrum Team do? Select the best option.

answers.text: Assign responsible team members for every improvement. Check the progress at the next Retrospective.
Make sure the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint includes all the improvements.
Make sure the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint includes at least one high priority process improvement.
Assign a responsible team member for at least one improvement. Check the progress at the next Retrospective.

explanation: The correct answer is « Make sure the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint includes at least one high priority process improvement. ». The Sprint Retrospective lets the Scrum Team inspect how it works — interactions, processes, tools, and its Definition of Done — and then plan the changes most useful to quality and effectiveness.

question: Who writes the Product Backlog Items?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Product Owner ». The Product Owner is accountable for making Product Backlog items clear and understandable. They may write them with Developers or stakeholders, but remain accountable for the clarity needed for Scrum Team decisions.

question: A Sprint can be cancelled by:
explanation: The correct answer is « The Product Owner ». Only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint, when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete. This authority protects the team from cancellations driven by simple pressure or a change of preference.

question: The Increment must be released at the end of every Sprint.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». An Increment is a concrete, usable, integrated step toward the Product Goal. It can be released once it meets the Definition of Done: the Sprint Review is not a release authorization.

question: What does transparency mean in Scrum?

answers.text: All information is visible to everyone.
All artifacts are visible to those inspecting them.
All Scrum events are open to everyone.
The work and progress are visible to all stakeholders.

explanation: The correct answer is « The work and progress are visible to all stakeholders. ». Scrum is founded on empiricism: decisions are based on what is observed. Transparency makes the state of work understandable; it enables useful inspection and then prompt adaptation when needed.

question: The Scrum Guide provides rules.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Scrum is a lightweight framework for addressing complex problems and creating value adaptively. The Scrum Guide defines the framework’s essential elements; it is purposely incomplete and does not prescribe a detailed process or one method.

question: Who owns the Sprint Backlog?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Developers ». The Sprint Backlog combines the Sprint Goal, the selected Product Backlog items, and the actionable plan for delivering the Increment. It is a plan by and for Developers, updated as they learn.

question: The Scrum Master is a servant leader.
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». The Scrum Master is a true leader who serves the Scrum Team and the organization. They help everyone understand Scrum, improve the team’s effectiveness, and act on impediments beyond the team’s direct control.

question: What is the purpose of the Daily Scrum?

answers.text: To provide status updates to the Product Owner.
To inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog accordingly.
To discuss problems encountered during the previous day.
To synchronize individual tasks for the next 24 hours.

explanation: The correct answer is « To inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog accordingly. ». The Daily Scrum is a fifteen-minute event for Developers. Its purpose is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the work plan; it is neither a status report to management nor a mandatory meeting for external parties.

question: How much business value is delivered in each Sprint?

answers.text: Determined by the Product Owner at the end of the Sprint.
Determined by the Stakeholders during the Sprint Review.
It's the sum of the value of all Product Backlog Items completed.
It's the amount of work completed and deemed 'Done'.

explanation: The correct answer is « It's the amount of work completed and deemed 'Done'. ». Value should be examined against the outcome sought for users, the organization, and the product, not merely the volume of features delivered. Product choices compare benefits, costs, risks, and available learning.

question: Which statement is true about the Product Goal?

answers.text: It is a detailed plan for the next release.
It is a short-term objective for a Sprint.
It describes a future state of the product which can serve as a target for the Scrum Team.
It is only used for new product development.

explanation: The correct answer is « It describes a future state of the product which can serve as a target for the Scrum Team. ». The Product Goal describes the intended future state of the product. It gives long-term direction to the Product Backlog and helps multiple teams converge on the same outcome; a new goal is taken on after the previous one is fulfilled or abandoned.

question: The Daily Scrum is a meeting of the Scrum Team, facilitated by the Scrum Master.

answers.text: The Developers solely participate with the Scrum Master facilitating.
All Scrum Team members must participate for 15 minutes or less.
Only the Developers and Product Owner attend.
The Scrum Master ensures the Developers meet the 15-minute timebox.

explanation: The correct answer is « The Developers solely participate with the Scrum Master facilitating. ». The Daily Scrum is a fifteen-minute event for Developers. Its purpose is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the work plan; it is neither a status report to management nor a mandatory meeting for external parties.

question: The Scrum Team has no hierarchy.
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». A Scrum Team includes one Product Owner, one Scrum Master, and Developers. There are no sub-teams or internal hierarchies: it is a cohesive unit accountable for creating value around one Product Goal.

question: Who is responsible for managing the Product Backlog?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Product Owner ». The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog. They make its content and ordering transparent so that decisions about value and the product’s next steps are understood by everyone.

question: Who creates the Definition of Done?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Developers ». The Definition of Done formally describes the quality state an Increment must meet. It creates a shared understanding of what is truly complete: an item that does not meet it is neither an Increment nor releasable work.

question: The Scrum Master must ensure that the Sprint Goal is met.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team understand and apply Scrum, but does not guarantee the Sprint Goal on its behalf. Developers adapt their plan toward that goal; the team learns when its forecast is not realized.

question: Scrum promotes self-managing teams.
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». Developers are self-managing: they internally decide who does what, when, and how to turn selected work into a usable Increment. The Product Owner defines the need and value, but does not prescribe the technical solution.

question: The Developers pull Product Backlog Items during the Sprint.
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». Developers select the work they believe they can complete to achieve the Sprint Goal. Work is therefore pulled according to their capacity and understanding, not pushed in from outside.

question: The Scrum Master must facilitate all Scrum Events.
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». The Scrum Master ensures that Scrum events take place, remain productive, and stay within their timebox. They do not turn them into management meetings: their purpose is to support transparency, inspection, and adaptation.

question: Which of the following is NOT a Scrum artifact?
explanation: The correct answer is « Sprint Goal ». The Sprint Goal is the Sprint’s single objective. It creates coherence and focus while leaving Developers flexibility about the precise work needed to achieve it; it does not guarantee that every initially selected item will be completed.

question: Who has the final say on the order of the Product Backlog?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Product Owner ». The Product Backlog is an ordered list, not merely a wish list. Its order makes value, risk, dependency, and learning choices visible; the Product Owner is accountable for it.

question: How much work should be selected for a Sprint?

answers.text: The Product Owner determines how much work to pull.
The Developers determine how much work to pull.
The Scrum Master determines how much work to pull.
The Scrum Team determines how much work to pull.

explanation: The correct answer is « The Developers determine how much work to pull. ». Developers are self-managing: they internally decide who does what, when, and how to turn selected work into a usable Increment. The Product Owner defines the need and value, but does not prescribe the technical solution.

question: What is Velocity?

answers.text: A measure of how fast the team is working.
A forecast of how much work the Developers can complete in a Sprint.
The sum of Product Backlog Items delivered in a Sprint.
A measure of the value delivered.

explanation: The correct answer is « A forecast of how much work the Developers can complete in a Sprint. ». Measures such as velocity or a burndown can help forecast, but they do not replace empiricism and are not a delivery commitment. Developers use capacity, their history, and the Definition of Done to make a realistic forecast.

question: What does it mean if the Increment is 'potentially shippable'?

answers.text: It is ready for User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and may have bugs.
It meets the Definition of Done and can be used by customers.
It means the Developers have finished their work on it, regardless of quality.
All tests have passed, but it still needs final approval.

explanation: The correct answer is « It meets the Definition of Done and can be used by customers. ». The Definition of Done formally describes the quality state an Increment must meet. It creates a shared understanding of what is truly complete: an item that does not meet it is neither an Increment nor releasable work.

question: Which of the following are Scrum events?
explanation: The correct answers are « Sprint Planning », « Daily Scrum », « Sprint Review » and « Sprint Retrospective ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: True or False: Product Backlog items are always detailed and refined at the same time.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Product Backlog items do not all have the same level of detail. Items closer to selection are generally more refined; Developers estimate the work because they will perform it.

question: Who is the 'facilitator'?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Scrum Master ». The Scrum Master facilitates Scrum when it is useful to do so: they help people collaborate effectively and keep events useful. Facilitating does not mean deciding or allocating work for the team.

question: Which statement best describes the role of management in Scrum?

answers.text: Managers are responsible for assigning tasks to Developers.
Managers determine the composition of the Scrum Team.
Managers support the Scrum Team by removing impediments and enabling self-management.

explanation: The correct answer is « Managers support the Scrum Team by removing impediments and enabling self-management. ». Developers are self-managing: they internally decide who does what, when, and how to turn selected work into a usable Increment. The Product Owner defines the need and value, but does not prescribe the technical solution.

question: Product Backlog items are always estimated by the Product Owner.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Product Owner does not always perform estimates. The Developers who will do the work are best placed to estimate it; the Product Owner contributes by clarifying value and trade-offs.

question: The Product Owner may delegate Product Backlog management to others.
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». The Product Owner may delegate some Product Backlog management activities, but not accountability. They remain accountable for value and for effective Product Backlog management.

question: All work to be performed during the Sprint is identified at Sprint Planning.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: Outcome over output is a key principle of Scrum.
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». Value should be examined against the outcome sought for users, the organization, and the product, not merely the volume of features delivered. Product choices compare benefits, costs, risks, and available learning.

question: Transparency in Scrum is achieved by:

answers.text: Making all artifacts visible and understood.

explanation: The correct answer is « Making all artifacts visible and understood. ». Scrum is founded on empiricism: decisions are based on what is observed. Transparency makes the state of work understandable; it enables useful inspection and then prompt adaptation when needed.

question: The Scrum Guide is definitive.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Scrum is a lightweight framework for addressing complex problems and creating value adaptively. The Scrum Guide defines the framework’s essential elements; it is purposely incomplete and does not prescribe a detailed process or one method.

question: What is the role of the Scrum Master?

answers.text: Ensure the team adheres to Scrum values and practices

explanation: The correct answer is « Ensure the team adheres to Scrum values and practices ». The Scrum values are Commitment, Focus, Openness, Respect, and Courage. They guide the behaviors that make transparency, inspection, and adaptation truly possible.

question: What are the responsibilities of the Development Team?

answers.text: Present the work at the Sprint Review

explanation: The correct answers are « Develop and test the product », « Present the work at the Sprint Review » and « Estimate user stories ». The Sprint Review is used to inspect the Sprint outcome, discuss progress toward the Product Goal, and decide useful adaptations. It is a working session with stakeholders, not merely a demonstration or a mandatory gate before release.

question: According to the Scrum Guide, what is the maximum duration of a Sprint?
explanation: The correct answer is « 1 month (4 weeks) ». A Sprint lasts at most one month. Its fixed length creates a regular rhythm for creating Increments, inspection, and adaptation; a team may choose a shorter Sprint.

question: Who is responsible for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Development Team?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Product Owner ». Value should be examined against the outcome sought for users, the organization, and the product, not merely the volume of features delivered. Product choices compare benefits, costs, risks, and available learning.

question: What are the three pillars of empiricism in Scrum?
explanation: The correct answers are « Transparency », « Inspection » and « Adaptation ». Scrum is founded on empiricism: decisions are based on what is observed. Transparency makes the state of work understandable; it enables useful inspection and then prompt adaptation when needed.

question: Which Scrum event has no time-box limit?

answers.text: None, all Scrum events have a time-box.

explanation: The correct answer is « None, all Scrum events have a time-box. ». All Scrum events have a maximum duration. A timebox creates a predictable cadence and prevents meetings from becoming longer without producing better decisions; the duration may be shorter when the purpose is met.

question: Who is responsible for creating the 'Done Increment' each Sprint?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Development Team ». Developers are accountable for creating a usable Increment that meets the Definition of Done. They determine the work and plan needed to achieve it during the Sprint.

question: What are the three questions the Scrum Guide gives as an example that can be used at the Daily Scrum?

answers.text: Do I have complete understanding of the Sprint Backlog item I am working on?
Did I explain all the discovered issues I found yesterday to the Product Owner?
What did I do yesterday that helped the Development Team meet the Sprint Goal?
What will do today to help the Development Team meet the Sprint Goal?
Do I see any impediment that prevents me or the Development Team from meeting the Sprint Goal?

explanation: The correct answers are « What did I do yesterday that helped the Development Team meet the Sprint Goal? », « What will do today to help the Development Team meet the Sprint Goal? » and « Do I see any impediment that prevents me or the Development Team from meeting the Sprint Goal? ». The Scrum Master helps cause the removal of impediments to the Scrum Team’s progress. They do not take work away from Developers: they facilitate resolution and help the organization when an impediment is beyond the team.

question: Who is allowed to change the Sprint Backlog during the Sprint?

answers.text: The Development Team and the Product Owner

explanation: The correct answer is « The Development Team ». The Sprint Backlog combines the Sprint Goal, the selected Product Backlog items, and the actionable plan for delivering the Increment. It is a plan by and for Developers, updated as they learn.

question: Who is allowed to make changes in the Product Backlog? Select two options.

answers.text: The Development Team, but with permission of the Product Owner

explanation: The correct answers are « The Product Owner » and « The Development Team, but with permission of the Product Owner ». Anyone may provide information or suggest a Product Backlog change, but the Product Owner remains accountable for its content and ordering. In this quiz’s wording, Developers may therefore make changes with the Product Owner’s permission.

question: How long should the Sprint Planning be?

answers.text: Until all the Items in the Sprint Backlog are decomposed to units of one day or less
Not more than 10% of the capacity of the Development Team

explanation: The correct answer is « Not more than 8 hours ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: What does the word "development" mean in the context of Scrum? Select the best option.

answers.text: Complex work that can include all the suggested options and even more
Research and identifying of viable markets, technologies, and Product capabilities
Product development, Its releasing and sustaining
Development of an operational environment for the Product

explanation: The correct answer is « Complex work that can include all the suggested options and even more ». In Scrum, “development” means any complex work needed to create or evolve a product: research, design, building, testing, operations, maintenance, or learning. It is not limited to software development.

question: What are the three pillars that uphold Scrum?
explanation: The correct answers are « Inspection », « Transparency » and « Adaptation ». Scrum is founded on empiricism: decisions are based on what is observed. Transparency makes the state of work understandable; it enables useful inspection and then prompt adaptation when needed.

question: What are Product Backlog features? Select three.

answers.text: As long as a product exists, its Product Backlog also exists
A Product Backlog could be closed when it contains no items to include into the next Sprint
When the final version of a product is rolled out, its Product Backlog is dismissed

explanation: The correct answers are « As long as a product exists, its Product Backlog also exists », « It is never complete » and « It is dynamic ». The Product Backlog is emergent and evolves for as long as the product exists. It does not need to contain all work before the first Sprint: feedback, risk, and opportunities change both its content and level of detail.

question: The Sprint Backlog is created at the Sprint Planning. It is prohibited to add new work into the Sprint Backlog later by the Development Team.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: How does the Scrum Master serve the Organization? Select the three most appropriate answers.

answers.text: Leading and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption
Planning Scrum implementations within the organization
Working with other Scrum Masters to increase the effectiveness of the application of Scrum in the organization
Mixing experienced developers and junior specialists across different Development Teams in the organization to speed up Scrum adoption
Making sure the key stakeholders are invited on all Scrum Reviews within organization

explanation: The correct answers are « Leading and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption », « Planning Scrum implementations within the organization » and « Working with other Scrum Masters to increase the effectiveness of the application of Scrum in the organization ». The Scrum Master also serves the organization: they help adopt Scrum, plan and support its implementation, and work with other Scrum Masters to increase its effectiveness. Their role therefore goes beyond the team’s meetings.

question: Who is responsible for all estimates in the Product Backlog?

answers.text: The Scrum Master and the Development Team
The Product owner and the Development Team
The Product owner and the Scrum Master

explanation: The correct answer is « The Development Team ». Product Backlog items do not all have the same level of detail. Items closer to selection are generally more refined; Developers estimate the work because they will perform it.

question: Who creates the increment?

answers.text: The Development Team and The Product Owner

explanation: The correct answer is « The Development Team ». Developers are accountable for creating a usable Increment that meets the Definition of Done. They determine the work and plan needed to achieve it during the Sprint.

question: Could the Sprint Planning be finished if only work planned for the first days of the Sprint is decomposed to units of one day or less?

answers.text: Yes, if the remaining work is also estimated, maybe in bigger units
No, all items in the Sprint Backlog should be decomposed to units of one day or less by the end of the Sprint Planning

explanation: The correct answer is « Yes, if the remaining work is also estimated, maybe in bigger units ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: The Development Team should be able to explain to the Product Owner and Scrum Master how it intends to work as a self-organizing team to accomplish the Sprint Goal and create the anticipated Increment.
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». Developers are self-managing: they internally decide who does what, when, and how to turn selected work into a usable Increment. The Product Owner defines the need and value, but does not prescribe the technical solution.

question: How does the Scrum Master help the Product Owner? Select the three most appropriate answers.

answers.text: Facilitating Scrum events as requested or needed
Finding techniques for effective Product Backlog management
Understanding product planning in an empirical environment
Leading and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption

explanation: The correct answers are « Facilitating Scrum events as requested or needed », « Finding techniques for effective Product Backlog management » and « Understanding product planning in an empirical environment ». The Scrum Master ensures that Scrum events take place, remain productive, and stay within their timebox. They do not turn them into management meetings: their purpose is to support transparency, inspection, and adaptation.

question: Scrum recommends using only those Scrum components and rules which suit most for a particular project.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Using only the Scrum elements one prefers changes the framework and hides problems. Scrum works as a whole; complementary practices may be added, but its essential elements must not be removed.

question: Who is responsible for crafting the Sprint Goal at the Sprint Planining?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Scrum Team ». The Sprint Goal is the Sprint’s single objective. It creates coherence and focus while leaving Developers flexibility about the precise work needed to achieve it; it does not guarantee that every initially selected item will be completed.

question: What provides guidance to the Development Team on why it is building the Increment?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Sprint Goal ». The Sprint Goal is the Sprint’s single objective. It creates coherence and focus while leaving Developers flexibility about the precise work needed to achieve it; it does not guarantee that every initially selected item will be completed.

question: How frequently should scrum users inspect Scrum artifacts and progress toward a Sprint Goal?

answers.text: Frequently, but it should not get in the way of the work

explanation: The correct answer is « As frequently as possible ». The Sprint Goal is the Sprint’s single objective. It creates coherence and focus while leaving Developers flexibility about the precise work needed to achieve it; it does not guarantee that every initially selected item will be completed.

question: Definition of Done can be reviewed and adapted during each Sprint Retrospective. True or False?
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». The Sprint Retrospective lets the Scrum Team inspect how it works — interactions, processes, tools, and its Definition of Done — and then plan the changes most useful to quality and effectiveness.

question: Could the Product Owner and the Scrum Master be a part of the Development Team?
explanation: The correct answer is « Yes ». Scrum accountabilities are distinct, even though one person may, depending on context, also contribute to development work. What matters is not confusing the accountabilities for value, Scrum effectiveness, and creating the Increment.

question: The Scrum Master does the following regarding the Daily Scrum (select all applicable variants):

answers.text: Teaches the Development Team to keep the Daily Scrum within the 15-minute time-box
If others are present at the Daily Scrum, ensures that they do not disrupt the meeting
Is responsible for conducting the Daily Scrum
Ensures that the Development Team has the meeting

explanation: The correct answers are « Teaches the Development Team to keep the Daily Scrum within the 15-minute time-box », « If others are present at the Daily Scrum, ensures that they do not disrupt the meeting » and « Ensures that the Development Team has the meeting ». The Scrum Master ensures that Scrum events take place, remain productive, and stay within their timebox. They do not turn them into management meetings: their purpose is to support transparency, inspection, and adaptation.

question: What are the three main qualities the team model in Scrum is designed to optimize?
explanation: The correct answers are « Flexibility », « Productivity » and « Creativity ». The Scrum team model seeks flexibility, creativity, and productivity. A small, cross-functional, self-managing team can learn, adapt, and create value without heavy hierarchical coordination.

question: How does the Scrum Master serve the Development Team? Select the three most appropriate answers.

answers.text: Helping the Development Team to create high-value products
Coaching the Development Team in self-organization and cross-functionality
Adding or removing developers from the Development Team in accordance with team velocity changes
Removing impediments to the Development Team's progress
Helping the Development Team as the team leader

explanation: The correct answers are « Helping the Development Team to create high-value products », « Coaching the Development Team in self-organization and cross-functionality » and « Removing impediments to the Development Team's progress ». Developers are self-managing: they internally decide who does what, when, and how to turn selected work into a usable Increment. The Product Owner defines the need and value, but does not prescribe the technical solution.

question: What are the characteristics of a Development Team? Select three most appropriate choices.

answers.text: Accountability belongs to the Development Team as a whole
Scrum recognizes no sub-teams in the Development Team
Having the Scrum Master as a part-time Developer in the Development Team
Scrum recognizes no titles for Development Team members
Having at least one test engineer in the Development Team

explanation: The correct answers are « Accountability belongs to the Development Team as a whole », « Scrum recognizes no sub-teams in the Development Team » and « Scrum recognizes no titles for Development Team members ». A Scrum Team includes one Product Owner, one Scrum Master, and Developers. There are no sub-teams or internal hierarchies: it is a cohesive unit accountable for creating value around one Product Goal.

question: Who participates in the Sprint Planning? Select three.
explanation: The correct answers are « The Product Owner », « The Scrum Master » and « The Development Team ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: What is the Sprint Backlog?

answers.text: The Product Backlog items selected for this Sprint plus the plan for delivering them
The plan for delivering Product Backlog Items
The Product Backlog items selected for this Sprint
The Product Backlog items selected for this Sprint plus the Team Backlog items

explanation: The correct answer is « The Product Backlog items selected for this Sprint plus the plan for delivering them ». The Sprint Backlog combines the Sprint Goal, the selected Product Backlog items, and the actionable plan for delivering the Increment. It is a plan by and for Developers, updated as they learn.

question: What comprises Scrum (select four)?
explanation: The correct answers are « Artifacts », « Events », « Rules » and « Roles ». Scrum comprises roles (now called accountabilities), events, artifacts, and the rules that bind them. Together these elements make empiricism operational.

question: What happens when a Sprint is cancelled? Select three.

answers.text: All incomplete Product Backlog Items are re-estimated and put back on the Product Backlog
If part of the work is potentially releasable, the Product Owner typically accepts it
Any completed and "Done" Product Backlog items are reviewed
At the Sprint Retrospective the Scrum Master determines who from the Development Team is responsible for cancelling the Sprint
Several top Product Backlog Items are taken into the Sprint Backlog to replace the obsolete items

explanation: The correct answers are « All incomplete Product Backlog Items are re-estimated and put back on the Product Backlog », « If part of the work is potentially releasable, the Product Owner typically accepts it » and « Any completed and "Done" Product Backlog items are reviewed ». The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management: the Product Goal, clear content, ordering, and transparency. They may ask for help or delegate activities, but accountability remains theirs.

question: All the Scrum Teams working on the same product should have the same Sprint length.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Scrum does not require teams working on the same product to have exactly the same Sprint length. A common cadence can simplify coordination, but the framework does not make it mandatory.

question: Where can Scrum be used? Check all the applicable items.

answers.text: Managing the operation of an organization
Development of almost everything we use in our daily lives as individuals and societies
Development and sustaining of Cloud and other operational environments
Research and identifying of viable markets, technologies, and product capabilities

explanation: The correct answers are « Managing the operation of an organization », « Development of almost everything we use in our daily lives as individuals and societies », « Development of products and enhancements », « Development of software and hardware », « Development and sustaining of Cloud and other operational environments » and « Research and identifying of viable markets, technologies, and product capabilities ». Scrum can be used in many domains whenever work is complex and learning through increments is useful: products, operations, software, hardware, research, or services. The framework is not limited to IT.

question: The structure of the Daily Scrum is well-defined and constant. Every team member should answer the three main questions: What did I do yesterday? What will I do today? Do I see any impediment?
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Scrum Master helps cause the removal of impediments to the Scrum Team’s progress. They do not take work away from Developers: they facilitate resolution and help the organization when an impediment is beyond the team.

question: Imagine the following situation. At the Sprint Retrospective meeting the Scrum Team identified some improvements that can be done. What should the Scrum Team do? Select the best option.

answers.text: Assign a responsible team member for at least one Improvement. Check the progress at the next Retrospective.
Assign responsible team members for every improvement. Check the progress at the next Retrospective.
Make sure the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint includes all the improvements.
Make sure the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint includes at least one high priority process Improvement.

explanation: The correct answer is « Make sure the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint includes at least one high priority process Improvement. ». The Sprint Retrospective lets the Scrum Team inspect how it works — interactions, processes, tools, and its Definition of Done — and then plan the changes most useful to quality and effectiveness.

question: How does Definition of "Done" help the Scrum Team? Select three most applicable items.

answers.text: DoD is used to assess when work is complete on the product Increment.
DoD guides the Development Team in knowing how many Product Backlog items it can select during a Sprint Planning.
DoD helps in inspection and adaptation
DoD helps to calculate velocity of the Scrum Team

explanation: The correct answers are « DoD is used to assess when work is complete on the product Increment. », « DoD guides the Development Team in knowing how many Product Backlog items it can select during a Sprint Planning. » and « DoD ensures artifact transparency. ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: What is the order of items in the Product Backlog?

answers.text: The less clear items at the top
The recently added items at the top
Less valuable and most unclear items at the bottom

explanation: The correct answer is « Less valuable and most unclear items at the bottom ». The Product Backlog is an ordered list, not merely a wish list. Its order makes value, risk, dependency, and learning choices visible; the Product Owner is accountable for it.

question: What are the three most applicable characteristics of the Product Owner?

answers.text: Lead Scrum evangelist in the Organization
Lead Facilitator of Key Stakeholder Involvement

explanation: The correct answers are « Product Marketplace Expert », « Lead Facilitator of Key Stakeholder Involvement » and « Product Value Maximizer ». Stakeholders provide essential information about value, context, and changing needs. The Scrum Team collaborates with them to learn and adapt the Product Backlog, while the Product Owner remains accountable for its decisions.

question: It is a good practice to have from time to time a special technical Sprint that consists only of tasks removing the technical debt without implementing any new functionality.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». A separate “hardening” or technical-only Sprint hides unfinished quality. Quality and technical debt should be addressed continuously so that each Increment can meet the Definition of Done and remain usable.

question: Who is responsible for tracking the total work remaining in the Sprint Backlog to project the likelihood of achieving the Sprint Goal?

answers.text: The Product Owner and the Development Team

explanation: The correct answer is « The Development Team ». The Sprint Goal is the Sprint’s single objective. It creates coherence and focus while leaving Developers flexibility about the precise work needed to achieve it; it does not guarantee that every initially selected item will be completed.

question: Definition of "Done" is created during the first Sprint and remains unchanged until the Product release.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Definition of Done formally describes the quality state an Increment must meet. It creates a shared understanding of what is truly complete: an item that does not meet it is neither an Increment nor releasable work.

question: Who is responsible for the Product Backlog?

answers.text: The Scrum Master and The Development Team
The Product Owner and The Scrum Master
The Product Owner and The Development Team

explanation: The correct answer is « The Product Owner ». The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog. They make its content and ordering transparent so that decisions about value and the product’s next steps are understood by everyone.

question: What does Cone of Uncertainty show?

answers.text: Hierarchy of tasks that comprise a project
How much work remains till the end of the Sprint
How much is known about the Product over time
Dependencies, start times and stop times for project tasks

explanation: The correct answer is « How much is known about the Product over time ». The Cone of Uncertainty illustrates that knowledge of the product grows over time. Forecasts therefore become more reliable as the team learns; it does not justify detailing or freezing the whole plan at the start.

question: It is normal to have a "hardening" Sprint to remove all technical debt and prepare the Product for upcoming release.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». An Increment is a concrete, usable, integrated step toward the Product Goal. It can be released once it meets the Definition of Done: the Sprint Review is not a release authorization.

question: The Daily Scrum time-box depends on the size of the Development team
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Daily Scrum is a fifteen-minute event for Developers. Its purpose is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the work plan; it is neither a status report to management nor a mandatory meeting for external parties.

question: The Scrum Team consists of
explanation: The correct answers are « The Scrum Master », « The Product Owner » and « The Development Team ». The Scrum Team is a cohesive, self-managing, cross-functional unit. It includes the Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developers: the two selected answers therefore describe complementary aspects of the same team.

question: What are the two essential features a Scrum Team should possess?

answers.text: It should be flexible enough to complete all the work planned for the Sprint even if some team members are on vacation
It should use tools, processes and techniques approved by the Organization
It should have all competencies needed to accomplish the work without depending on others not part of the team
It should choose how best to accomplish their work, rather than being directed by others outside the team

explanation: The correct answers are « It should have all competencies needed to accomplish the work without depending on others not part of the team » and « It should choose how best to accomplish their work, rather than being directed by others outside the team ». A Scrum Team should be able to create value without continually depending on people outside it: it is cross-functional. It must also choose for itself how to accomplish its work: it is self-managing.

question: What is Scrum?

answers.text: A sequential design process, used in software development processes, in which progress is seen as flowing steadily downwards
A framework within which people can address complex adaptive problems, while delivering valuable products
A software development methodology which is intended to improve software quality

explanation: The correct answer is « A framework within which people can address complex adaptive problems, while delivering valuable products ». Scrum is a lightweight framework for addressing complex problems and creating value adaptively. The Scrum Guide defines the framework’s essential elements; it is purposely incomplete and does not prescribe a detailed process or one method.

question: Who is responsible for coping with incomplete artifact transparency?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Scrum Master ». Scrum is founded on empiricism: decisions are based on what is observed. Transparency makes the state of work understandable; it enables useful inspection and then prompt adaptation when needed.

question: What are the time-boxes for the Sprint Review and the Sprint Retrospective?
explanation: The correct answer is « 4 and 3 hours respectively ». The Sprint Review is used to inspect the Sprint outcome, discuss progress toward the Product Goal, and decide useful adaptations. It is a working session with stakeholders, not merely a demonstration or a mandatory gate before release.

question: What could be a source of requirements for any changes to be made to the product?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Product Backlog ». The Product Backlog makes visible the needs and improvements considered for the product. It is therefore the source of work from which the Scrum Team can discuss, order, and select product changes.

question: What is the essence of Scrum? Select the most appropriate option.

answers.text: A small team of people that is highly flexible and adaptive
The Scrum Master and the Product Owner

explanation: The correct answer is « A small team of people that is highly flexible and adaptive ». Scrum is a lightweight framework for addressing complex problems and creating value adaptively. The Scrum Guide defines the framework’s essential elements; it is purposely incomplete and does not prescribe a detailed process or one method.

question: Scrum is not a process or technique. True or False?
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». Scrum is a lightweight framework for addressing complex problems and creating value adaptively. The Scrum Guide defines the framework’s essential elements; it is purposely incomplete and does not prescribe a detailed process or one method.

question: What are the Scrum Artifacts? Select all applicable items.
explanation: The correct answers are « Product Backlog », « Sprint Backlog » and « Increment ». The Sprint Backlog combines the Sprint Goal, the selected Product Backlog items, and the actionable plan for delivering the Increment. It is a plan by and for Developers, updated as they learn.

question: Who is responsible for promoting and supporting Scrum? Select the best choice.

answers.text: The Scrum Master and the Product Owner

explanation: The correct answer is « The Scrum Master ». The Scrum Master also serves the organization: they help adopt Scrum, plan and support its implementation, and work with other Scrum Masters to increase its effectiveness. Their role therefore goes beyond the team’s meetings.

question: Who is allowed to participate in the Daily Scrum?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Development Team ». The Daily Scrum is a fifteen-minute event for Developers. Its purpose is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the work plan; it is neither a status report to management nor a mandatory meeting for external parties.

question: Check all the formal opportunities to inspect and adapt.
explanation: The correct answers are « The Sprint Planning », « The Daily Scrum », « The Sprint Review » and « The Sprint Retrospective ». Scrum events provide the formal opportunities to inspect and adapt: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, and Sprint Retrospective. Each addresses a different object — plan, progress, outcome, or way of working — and all reinforce empiricism.

question: What is the result of the Sprint Review?

answers.text: Common understanding of progress toward the Sprint Goal and how progress is tending toward completing the work in the Sprint Backlog
A list of improvements that the Scrum Team will implement in the next Sprint
Common understanding of what can be delivered in the Increment and how will the work needed to deliver the Increment be achieved
A revised Product Backlog that defines the probable Product Backlog items for the next Sprint

explanation: The correct answer is « A revised Product Backlog that defines the probable Product Backlog items for the next Sprint ». The Sprint Review is used to inspect the Sprint outcome, discuss progress toward the Product Goal, and decide useful adaptations. It is a working session with stakeholders, not merely a demonstration or a mandatory gate before release.

question: Who has the authority to cancel the Sprint?

answers.text: The Product Owner and the Scrum Master

explanation: The correct answer is « The Product Owner ». Only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel a Sprint, and only when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete. It is not a mechanism for reacting to every difficulty or priority change.

question: Who is responsible for monitoring progress toward high-level goals?

answers.text: The Product Owner and The Development Team
The Scrum Master and The Development Team

explanation: The correct answer is « The Product Owner ». The Product Owner monitors progress toward higher-level product goals. They use the Product Backlog’s state, Increments, and feedback to adapt value choices and product direction.

question: Scrum does not allow additional meetings that are not defined in Scrum
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Scrum events are the minimum formal events needed for empiricism. The team may arrange other discussions when useful; Scrum primarily seeks to avoid unnecessary meetings and preserve time for creating value.

question: What does Burn-down Chart show?

answers.text: Hierarchy of tasks that comprise a project
How much work remains till the end of the Sprint
The evolution of the amount of uncertainty during a project
Dependencies, start times and stop times for project tasks

explanation: The correct answer is « How much work remains till the end of the Sprint ». Measures such as velocity or a burndown can help forecast, but they do not replace empiricism and are not a delivery commitment. Developers use capacity, their history, and the Definition of Done to make a realistic forecast.

question: Other people than the Scrum Team can attend the Sprint Planning in order to provide technical or domain advice
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: What part of the capacity of the Development Team does Product Backlog refinement usually consume?

answers.text: The Development Team is not authorized for Product Backlog refinement

explanation: The correct answer is « Not more than 10% ». Refinement is an ongoing activity: Product Backlog items are broken down and clarified until they are transparent and small enough to be selected in Sprint Planning. It is neither a separate Scrum event nor a phase reserved for the Product Owner.

question: Imagine you are a Scrum Master in a small Organization that tries to adopt Scrum. There are 10 developers and one Product Owner. How can they be divided into teams? Choose all applicable options:

answers.text: 1 team of 10 people (because there is no reason to divide)
2 teams of 6 and 4 people (because it is good to have a separate QA team)
2 teams of 5 and 5 people (after a short meeting the developers decided this is the best option)
3 teams of 4, 3 and 3 people (each team is cross-functional)

explanation: The correct answers are « 2 teams of 5 and 5 people (after a short meeting the developers decided this is the best option) » and « 3 teams of 4, 3 and 3 people (each team is cross-functional) ». The Product Owner is one person, not a committee. They may represent the needs of many stakeholders, but their Product Backlog decisions remain coherent and visible to the whole Scrum Team.

question: What does Product Backlog management include? Select three most applicable items.

answers.text: Optimizing the value of the work the Development Team performs
Moving Product Backlog items into the Sprint Backlog
Ordering the items in the Product Backlog to best achieve goals and missions
Presenting Product Backlog items to the Key Stakeholders
Ensuring that the Product Backlog is visible, transparent, and clear to all, and shows what the Scrum Team will work on next

explanation: The correct answers are « Optimizing the value of the work the Development Team performs », « Ordering the items in the Product Backlog to best achieve goals and missions » and « Ensuring that the Product Backlog is visible, transparent, and clear to all, and shows what the Scrum Team will work on next ». The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the Scrum Team’s work. They do not direct Developers: they provide product direction and make value choices and Product Backlog ordering clear.

question: If an item in the Sprint Backlog cannot be finished by the end of the Sprint (if it turned out there is a lot more work to do than was estimated), the Sprint is cancelled.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Sprint Backlog combines the Sprint Goal, the selected Product Backlog items, and the actionable plan for delivering the Increment. It is a plan by and for Developers, updated as they learn.

question: Who participates in the Sprint Review? Select all applicable variants.
explanation: The correct answers are « The Scrum Master », « The Development Team », « The Key Stakeholders » and « The Product Owner ». The Sprint Review is used to inspect the Sprint outcome, discuss progress toward the Product Goal, and decide useful adaptations. It is a working session with stakeholders, not merely a demonstration or a mandatory gate before release.

question: What is the time-box for the Daily Scrum?

answers.text: Not limited. Every Development Team member should have enough time to answer the three Main Questions

explanation: The correct answer is « 15 minutes ». The Daily Scrum is a fifteen-minute event for Developers. Its purpose is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the work plan; it is neither a status report to management nor a mandatory meeting for external parties.

question: What is the Sprint Retrospective?

answers.text: It is a meeting where the Development Team synchronizes activities and creates a plan for the next 24 hours
It is a meeting to inspect the Increment and adapt the Product Backlog if needed
It is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself and create a plan for improvements to be enacted during the next Sprint
It is the key inspect and adapt meeting

explanation: The correct answer is « It is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself and create a plan for improvements to be enacted during the next Sprint ». The Sprint Retrospective lets the Scrum Team inspect how it works — interactions, processes, tools, and its Definition of Done — and then plan the changes most useful to quality and effectiveness.

question: The purpose of the Sprint Retrospective is to (select three):

answers.text: Inspect how the last Sprint went with regards to people, interactions, process and tools
Identify and order the major items that went well and potential improvements
Create a plan for implementing improvements in the way the Scrum Team does its work
Get technical or domain advice from specialists invited by The Development Team or The Scrum Master
Get feedback from the Key Stakeholders invited by the Product Owner

explanation: The correct answers are « Inspect how the last Sprint went with regards to people, interactions, process and tools », « Identify and order the major items that went well and potential improvements » and « Create a plan for implementing improvements in the way the Scrum Team does its work ». The Sprint Retrospective lets the Scrum Team inspect how it works — interactions, processes, tools, and its Definition of Done — and then plan the changes most useful to quality and effectiveness.

question: Select the five Scrum Values
explanation: The correct answers are « Courage », « Commitment », « Openness », « Focus » and « Respect ». Listening to technical concerns, making them visible, and adjusting Product Backlog ordering demonstrates Respect and Openness. The Product Owner recognizes Developers’ expertise and adapts value decisions using transparent information.

question: What should be taken into account for the Definition of "Done"? Select the two most appropriate items

answers.text: Definition of "Done" of other Scrum Teams working on other products
Definition of "Done" of other Scrum Teams working on the same Product
Conventions, standards and guidelines of the organization

explanation: The correct answers are « Definition of "Done" of other Scrum Teams working on the same Product » and « Conventions, standards and guidelines of the organization ». The Definition of Done formally describes the quality state an Increment must meet. It creates a shared understanding of what is truly complete: an item that does not meet it is neither an Increment nor releasable work.

question: If an inspector determines that one or more aspects of a process deviate outside acceptable limits, when must an adjustment be made?

answers.text: As soon as possible to minimize further deviation
The deviations should be discussed at the Daily Scrum and then an adjustment must be made
After clarifying all the details with the Product Owner

explanation: The correct answer is « As soon as possible to minimize further deviation ». As soon as inspection reveals an unacceptable deviation, adaptation should be made as soon as possible. Waiting increases the cost of the problem and reduces the team’s ability to control risk.

question: What is the input to the Sprint Planning? Select four

answers.text: Projected capacity of the Development Team during the Sprint
Past performance of the Development Team

explanation: The correct answers are « The Product Backlog », « The latest product Increment », « Projected capacity of the Development Team during the Sprint » and « Past performance of the Development Team ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: What are the questions the Sprint Planning answers? Select two

answers.text: How will the work needed to deliver the Increment be achieved?
What can be delivered in the Increment resulting from the upcoming Sprint?
What new technologies could be used to speed up the Development Team velocity?
Who will be responsible for each item in the Sprint Backlog?
What is the size of the Technical Debt and how could it be removed?

explanation: The correct answers are « How will the work needed to deliver the Increment be achieved? » and « What can be delivered in the Increment resulting from the upcoming Sprint? ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: The Daily Scrum always should take exactly 15 minutes. For example, if your team managed doing it in 5 minutes, you should spend 10 more minutes on some useful team activity like Product Backlog refinement, but not more
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Refinement is an ongoing activity: Product Backlog items are broken down and clarified until they are transparent and small enough to be selected in Sprint Planning. It is neither a separate Scrum event nor a phase reserved for the Product Owner.

question: In which meetings the Key Stakeholders are allowed to participate?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Sprint Review ». The Sprint Review is used to inspect the Sprint outcome, discuss progress toward the Product Goal, and decide useful adaptations. It is a working session with stakeholders, not merely a demonstration or a mandatory gate before release.

question: The Scrum Master is focused primarily on the Scrum Team and usually does not care about those outside the Scrum Team.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team as well as the Product Owner and the organization. In particular, they help remove barriers between stakeholders and teams; they are therefore not limited to the team’s internal scope.

question: Only the Product Owner and the Development Team participate in the Sprint Planning. There is nothing to do for the Scrum Master
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: Who is responsible for creation of the Definition of "Done"?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Development Team ». The Definition of Done formally describes the quality state an Increment must meet. It creates a shared understanding of what is truly complete: an item that does not meet it is neither an Increment nor releasable work.

question: What belongs solely to the Development Team?
explanation: The correct answer is « The Sprint Backlog ». The Sprint Backlog combines the Sprint Goal, the selected Product Backlog items, and the actionable plan for delivering the Increment. It is a plan by and for Developers, updated as they learn.

question: What is the Increment?

answers.text: The sum of all the Product Backlog items completed during the Sprint
The sum of all the Product Backlog items completed during the Sprint and the value of the Increments of all previous Sprints
All Items in the Sprint Backlog that could be released regardless of whether the Product Owner decides to actually do it
All "Done" items in the Sprint Backlog

explanation: The correct answer is « The sum of all the Product Backlog items completed during the Sprint and the value of the Increments of all previous Sprints ». Value should be examined against the outcome sought for users, the organization, and the product, not merely the volume of features delivered. Product choices compare benefits, costs, risks, and available learning.

question: All Development Teams working on the same Product should use the same Product Backlog.
explanation: The correct answer is « True ». Teams working on the same product use one Product Backlog. This preserves a single source of transparency and lets the Product Owner order work toward one product direction.

question: Scrum is founded on
explanation: The correct answer is « Empiricism ». Scrum is founded on empiricism: decisions are based on what is observed. Transparency makes the state of work understandable; it enables useful inspection and then prompt adaptation when needed.

question: What happens during the Sprint? Select three answers.

answers.text: No changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal
Sprint scope is defined at the Sprint Planning and cannot be changed
The Sprint Goal is changed frequently to reflect the status of the remaining work
Scope may be clarified and re-negotiated between the Product Owner and Development Team as more is learned

explanation: The correct answers are « No changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal », « Quality goals do not decrease » and « Scope may be clarified and re-negotiated between the Product Owner and Development Team as more is learned ». During the Sprint, no change may endanger the Sprint Goal. Scope can be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as the team learns, without reducing quality.

question: It is a good practice to have at least two Product Owners on big projects.
explanation: The correct answer is « False ». Even for a large product, Scrum provides for one Product Owner to preserve unambiguous direction and Product Backlog ordering. They may be helped by other people, but do not become a committee of Product Owners.

question: Select the two meetings in which people outside the Scrum Team are allowed to participate.
explanation: The correct answers are « The Sprint Review » and « The Sprint Planning ». Sprint Planning is collaborative work by the whole Scrum Team. It addresses three questions: why the Sprint is valuable, which items can be done, and how Developers plan to complete them.

question: Is it allowed to skip the Daily Scrum if there is nothing interesting to talk about?
explanation: The correct answer is « No ». The Daily Scrum is a fifteen-minute event for Developers. Its purpose is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the work plan; it is neither a status report to management nor a mandatory meeting for external parties.
